clue.text: (& 13ac.) Eye, say, spikes crooked deal – artificial exercise for politicians etc. beset by scandal?

definitions.text: exercise for politicians etc. beset by scandal

indicators.note: to spike something is to drive into it, so one piece is driven inside the other
something crooked is bent out of its straight order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Private Eye is an example of a magazine, a mag
imitation leather is artificial leather

explanation.surface: The magazine itself barges in on a dodgy deal, leaving scandal-hit politicians scrambling to cover up.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye, the satirical magazine running this puzzle, is the 'Eye'. The anagram is split around the inserted piece rather than kept whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Damage limitation is the effort to minimise harm, the spin operation any politician caught in a scandal mounts.

clue.text: House members do Democrat good and proper

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for Democrat
well means properly or thoroughly, as in done good and proper

explanation.surface: A Democrat in the House of Representatives is praised for doing a thorough, decent job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House members' suggests Congress; it really means the people living in a house, and what they do there.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to live in a place, which is exactly what the occupants of a home do.

clue.text: Body aimed to shake up newspapers etc.

indicators.note: shaking something up scrambles its contents, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a mass is a body of matter
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Some organisation sets out to disrupt the newspaper industry.
explanation.definitionFit: The mass media are the press, television and radio, with newspapers the classic example.

clue.text: Young man kept squeezing end of tool between rings after engagement

indicators.note: squeezing something holds it tightly, so one piece sits inside another
between places a letter in the gap with something on either side of it
the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept
after places one part behind another in the reading order

blocks.note: a gig is a performer's booking or engagement
rings are round, so each is the letter O
the final letter of tool

explanation.surface: A kept young man, tight hold of a tool, with rings involved after getting engaged: a smutty little scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigolo is a young man paid or supported by an older lover, a kept man.

clue.text: Prat welcomes back member at end of debate going on for ever

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the outer word holds the others
going back means reading the word from right to left
the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

a leg is a limb, a member of the body
the final letter of debate

explanation.surface: Some fool lets a member back in just as a debate that seemed endless finally winds up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' tempts towards MP, but here it is a limb; prat is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ageless never grows old, so it seems to continue eternally.

clue.text: Balls and other members, finally socialist, embraced by Neil, sag pathetically

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the following word
done pathetically means done badly and out of order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the last letter of socialist
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Neil Kinnock and Ed Balls as Labour 'members' sagging feebly in an embrace, a Private Eye smut joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced by' sounds like a container, but the final T simply joins the letters of NEIL SAG in one anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Genitals are the sexual organs, the testicles and the 'member' among them.

clue.text: Insult Balls, ultimately dismissed as "easy to pick up"

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word before it
dismissed means sent away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: a slight is an insult or snub
the last letter of Balls

explanation.surface: Ed Balls, the Labour politician, gets brushed off as a pushover.
explanation.walkthrough: SLIGHT loses its S to leave LIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something light weighs little, so lifting it requires hardly any effort.

clue.text: Conference: I'm pussy-whipped (Mo being involved)

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, joining the letters to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'pussy-whipped' looks like one word; 'whipped' is split off as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A symposium is a meeting or conference for discussion of a particular subject.

clue.text: MPs talk of Mates condom distribution to include, initially, errant bishop

the first letter of errant

explanation.walkthrough: Mates is a British condom brand. The Commons is the House of Commons, Britain's elected chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: A Commons debate is a discussion between MPs in the House of Commons.

clue.text: see 28ac.
Madcap rowing wife goes for genital area

blocks.note: taken as written

clue.text: see 26ac.

clue.text: see 1ac.

explanation.definitionFit: A birthmark is a blemish on the skin, a literal stigma or mark.

clue.text: Drug to be taken via one's arse, say, backwards (yes, that's what it says)

explanation.definitionFit: An analgesic is a painkilling medicine.

clue.text: Brief tingle he produced, core of penis

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the middle letter of penis

explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like it shortens tingle, but it is the definition, a verb; all of TINGLE goes in.

clue.text: Act like certain Welsh members having the power to cover up shit?

explanation.walkthrough: The Welsh Assembly (now the Senedd) is the devolved parliament of Wales; its members assemble.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble is to gather together, which is what Assembly members do when they convene.

clue.text: Blast the non-PC female party!

a side is a party in a dispute

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blast!' reads as a curse, but here it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadside is a full volley of a warship's guns, or a fierce verbal attack, a blast.

first letters of these three words
